stem: Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a common organic solvent and reagent.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Propanone reacts with methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$, under acidic conditions to form compound $\text{A}$, as shown by reaction 1.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 2.1

reaction 1 $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + 2\text{CH}_3\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+}$  $+ \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The overall order of reaction 1 can be found by studying experimental data.

Table 2.1 shows how the initial rate of reaction changes as $[\text{CH}_3\text{OH}]$ and $[\text{H}^+]$ are varied. In each experiment, a large excess of $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ is used.

Table 2.1

| experiment | $[\text{CH}_3\text{OH}]$ / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{H}^+]$ / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | relative initial rate of reaction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 0.010 | 0.010 | 1.00 |
| 2 | 0.015 | 0.015 | 2.25 |
| 3 | 0.015 | 0.020 | 3.00 |
parts.text: Explain why a large excess of $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ is used in each experiment.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Use the data in Table 2.1 to determine the order of reaction 1 with respect to $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ and to $\text{H}^+$ ions. Explain your answers.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
In a separate experiment, a large excess of $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ and $\text{H}^+$ ions are added to a solution containing a known concentration of $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$.

Fig. 2.2 shows how $[\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3]$ varies over time.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Fig. 2.2

Use Fig. 2.2 to show how, under these conditions, reaction 1 is first order with respect to $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Propanone also reacts with acidified cyanide ions to form the hydroxynitrile compound $\text{B}$, as shown by reaction 2. {{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}} Fig. 2.3 reaction 2 $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{H}^+ + \text{CN}^- \longrightarrow$ The following rate equation is determined for reaction 2. $$\text{rate} = k[\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3][\text{H}^+]$$ Four possible mechanisms for reaction 2 are shown in Table 2.2. Table 2.2 | proposed reaction mechanism | steps | | :--- | :--- | | 1 | fast $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow [\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)CH}_3]^+$
slow $[\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)CH}_3]^+ + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_3$ | | 2 | fast $\text{H}^+ + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{HCN}$
slow $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_3$ | | 3 | slow $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(O}^-\text{)(CN)CH}_3$
fast $\text{CH}_3\text{C(O}^-\text{)(CN)CH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_3$ | | 4 | slow $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow [\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)CH}_3]^+$
fast $[\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)CH}_3]^+ + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_3$ | Suggest which of these mechanisms is consistent with the rate equation for reaction 2. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Carboxylic acid $\text{C}$, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_3$, forms when $\text{B}$ is hydrolysed under hot acidic conditions.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The $pK_{\text{a}}$ of $\text{C}$ is 3.95. Calculate the pH of a $0.500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of $\text{C}$.

Show your working.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{C}$ can be used to form buffer solution $\text{D}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Buffer solution $\text{D}$ is made when $20.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $1.00\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ is added to $100\text{ cm}^3$ of a $0.500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of $\text{C}$.

The $pK_{\text{a}}$ of $\text{C}$ is 3.95.

Calculate the pH of buffer solution $\text{D}$.

Show your working.
